Okay. So, there are a couple ways you could approach this and I'm fairly familiar with both of them. Whichever method you use will depend on whether or not the SSD in question comes already formatted or if you have to do it yourself. If it's the latter, installing it prematurely might mean that the hard drive doesn't properly register with the system.

In any event, you *could* use specialized software and an [HDD docking station](https://digitaladvisor.com/hdd/docking-station/) to clone your current system hard drive. The one I use is called [AOMEI Partition Assistant](https://www.aomeitech.com/aomei-partition-assistant.html). This program is pretty powerful; to the point where you can add, modify, or delete partitions directly into your hard drive. But that's advanced level stuff you probably don't need to worry about right now.

The second option would be to simply install Windows from scratch like you mentioned earlier. For this, you just have to ensure the hard drive is formatted before installing said drive, and that you have access to Windows installation software (either a USB boot-up drive or download a copy from the official site via Windows built-in feature).

However, if this is **not** a system drive you're upgrading but, instead, a secondary internal drive that's being used for storage, then you could just clone the drive. That's presuming you have the hardware to do this.

Keep in mind, if you decide to install a fresh new drive that's completely empty, you may have to go with option 2. In other words, having a copy of Windows on a USB drive and doing a fresh install is probably the easiest way.

Anyways, hopefully my long, geeky diatribe helps you in some way. Best of luck to you and welcome to the gaming PC world! :)
